title: SDK: Embeddings & Rerank — unified pagination, batching, and retry ergonomics across Python/TS/Go
creator: Maya Chen
description: Deliver a consistent, ergonomic set of SDK primitives for embeddings + reranking workflows across Python, TypeScript, and Go. Work includes: pagination helpers for streaming large embedding result sets, batching helper utilities for client-side grouping of small requests, explicit retry/backoff policies aligned with platform rate limits, and idiomatic streaming ergonomics (async iterators in TS/Python, channels in Go). The goal is API parity so customers can port workload examples between languages with minimal cognitive overhead.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs expose a unified EmbeddingsClient.paginate_embeddings or equivalent across languages
Batching helper available that accepts size/byte limits and returns batched payloads (examples in README)
Retry/backoff configurable per-client and default to platform-recommended jittered exponential backoff
Streaming ergonomics documented: async iterator example in Python/TS and channel/iterator example in Go
Integration tests demonstrating parity for a 10k-item embedding + rerank flow (end-to-end smoke tests)
Docs and quickstarts updated with cross-language snippets and migration notes
technical_notes: Design choice: client-side batching helper vs server-side auto-batching. We'll ship client helper first (faster iteration) and expose server-side hints later.
Retries: default policy = exp backoff with full jitter, initial=150ms, max=5s, max_attempts=5. Expose policy object in each SDK so advanced users can inject burst-aware logic.
Pagination: cursor-based for embeddings/rerank list endpoints. SDK provides high-level paginated iterator and low-level page extractor for advanced control.

Streaming: Python and TS use async generators to yield partial embedding/score chunks. Go uses a channel + context cancellation pattern. Ensure memory-boundedness by streaming items instead of materializing the entire response.
Batch signature examples: BatchHelper(batch_size:int, max_bytes:int, truncate_fn:callable) -> yields list[items]. For TS/Go, adapt types to language conventions.
Backward compatibility: preserve existing EmbeddingsClient.embed_batch signature; new helpers are opt-in to avoid breaking changes. Provide deprecation plan if we unify signatures later.
updates: 2026-03-11: Spike completed — prototype batching helper in python and ts. Observed ~22% token-cost reduction for small-requests workload when using 16-item batches.

2026-03-12: Cross-SDK API review with DX and Go owner. Agreement on API surface: PaginatedIterator + BatchHelper + RetryPolicy. Action: add Go idiomatic wrapper (context + channel) — assigned to Nora Li (ENG-8330).

2026-03-13: PRs opened (links above). Python PR includes async iterator and sync wrapper for users not using asyncio. Integration smoke test added to CI that runs 1k-item embedding pagination with mocked rate-limits.
Next: finalize docs and examples, run cross-language e2e with internal benchmark harness, and schedule a small beta with two customers using Dedicated capacity.

example_snippets: Python async pagination example: async for vec in EmbeddingsClient.paginate(query_items, batch_size=16): process(vec)
TS async iterator: for await (const page of EmbeddingsClient.paginate(inputs, {batchSize:16})) { page.items.forEach(...)}
Go channel pattern: ch := client.Paginate(ctx, inputs, Opts{BatchSize:16}); for item := range ch { process(item) }
Batch helper usage: for batch in BatchHelper(items, batch_size=8, max_bytes=51200) -> send embed request and collect responses
Retry usage: client = NewClient(WithRetryPolicy(DefaultRetryPolicy())) or WithRetryPolicy(CustomPolicy{Initial:200, Max:6000, Attempts:6})
